hero.title: Google's Ranking Pipeline: From Crawl to SERP
hero.subtitle: The DOJ trial revealed Google's complete ranking architecture: a modular pipeline from crawling through indexing, retrieval, scoring, and multiple re-ranking stages. 100+ raw signals are combined via linear weighted formulas into three top-level scores (Q*, P*, T*), then refined by Twiddlers and ML systems.

keyInsight.label: Key Insight from DOJ Trial
keyInsight.text: Only RankBrain and DeepRank use LLM/ML technologies. All other ranking signals are hand-crafted (HJ Kim deposition). 100+ raw signals are combined via linear weighted formulas into top-level scores. Sigmoid functions and threshold engineering handle signal blending. 16,000 human raters score IS (0-100) which trains RankBrain, SpamBrain, HelpfulContent, and MUM.

pillars.title: 2 Patents
items: 0-1 scale, query-independent
Hand-crafted, not ML
Feeds: NSR, siteAuthority, OriginalContentScore, EffortScore
Below 0.4: ineligible for rich results
Represents domain trustworthiness
US9734211: Personalizing search results; US7783639: Determining quality of linked documents

pillars.title: User Interaction Signals
items: Combines NavBoost click data with anchor metrics
goodClicks, badClicks, lastLongestClicks
Chrome data: visits, scrolls, form submissions
directFrac: brand/type-in traffic fraction
13 months of click data retention

pillars.title: Query-Document Relevance
items: Three sub-signals: Anchors, Body, Clicks
A: "What the web says about a document" (anchor text)
B: "What the document says about itself" (on-page content)
C: Click-based topicality from user behavior
QBST memorizes words on relevant pages

100+ raw signals with aggregate top-level scores (PXR0357, Nayak Jan 2025): Google uses over 100 raw signals. Top-level signals are aggregates of other raw signals. Combines into a single score determining document rank ('Final IR')

Debugging interface reveals pipeline (PXR0357): Internal debugging interface shows query expansion/decomposition and table of blue links with scores per top-level signal. Engineers can inspect how each signal contributes to final ranking

Google avoids predicting clicks (PXR0357): Google avoids simply 'predicting clicks' because clicks are easily manipulated and a poor proxy for user experience. Deliberate design choice to not optimize ranking directly for click prediction

pillars.title: Ranking Impact and Secrecy
items: Ranking is an 'extreme outlier' in business impact (UPX0219, Eric Lehman May 2020): 'Ranking is an extreme outlier in business impact.' Ranking changes directly affect Google's core revenue

Search features depend on web results (UPX0219): 'Many search features use web results to understand what a query is about and trigger accordingly.' Web ranking is the foundation for other Google products
Search technology spreads across Google (UPX0219): 'Technologies developed in search spread out across the company to Ads, YouTube, Play.' Search ranking R&D is Google's core competitive advantage

Manipulation attempts are well-funded (UPX0204, Eric Lehman Nov 2018): 'Attempts to manipulate search results are continuous, sophisticated, and well-funded.' Internal acknowledgment of the SEO arms race
Click secrecy policy (UPX0204): 'Do not discuss the use of clicks in search, except on a need-to-know basis. Google has a public position.' Deliberate policy to hide click signal usage from public
Political bias secrecy (UPX0204): 'Do not discuss political bias in search in writing.' Internal policy to avoid written documentation of political bias considerations

pillarsExtra.title: Process Hundreds of URLs
items: Run before main scoring on larger candidate set
PredocTwiddlers - Apply broad filters and boosters
DMCAFilter - Remove copyright-infringing content
BadURLsCategorizer - Filter problematic URLs
BlogCategorizer - Identify and classify blog content

pillarsExtra.title: Refine Top 20-30 Results
items: Run on final candidate set only (expensive operations)
FreshnessTwiddler - Boost fresh content for time-sensitive queries
QualityBoost - Boost high-quality results
OfficialPageTwiddler - Boost official/brand pages
YouTubeDensityTwiddler - Control YouTube result proportion

pillarsExtra.title: Neural Refinement
items: RankEmbed - Dual encoder with dot product similarity (not cosine)
Trained on exactly 70 days of search logs + human rater scores
DeepRank - Decomposable BERT/Transformer analysis
RankBrain - Query understanding for novel queries
16,000 raters score IS (0-100) to train these systems

pillarsExtra.title: How the Ranking Pipeline Affects Your SEO
items: Optimize for each pipeline stage sequentially: Your page must survive Mustang retrieval (T* topicality), Ascorer scoring (Q* + P* + T*), PredocTwiddlers (dedup, diversity), LazyTwiddlers (quality boost, freshness), NavBoost (click re-ranking), and ML refinement (RankEmbed, DeepRank). A page with perfect content but no click engagement fails at NavBoost. A page with great clicks but poor topicality fails at Mustang. Diagnose which stage is filtering you out.

Balance across Q*, P*, and T* rather than over-optimizing one: The linear weighted formula combines 100+ signals into three top-level scores. No single signal dominates (HJ Kim deposition). A page with excellent T* (topicality) but zero P* (popularity/engagement) will lose to a page with moderate scores across all three. Distribute optimization effort: content relevance (T*), site quality and trust (Q*), and user engagement signals (P*).

Target OfficialPageTwiddler for brand queries: LazyTwiddlers include OfficialPageTwiddler, which boosts official brand pages in the top 20-30 results. For your own brand terms, ensure your homepage and key landing pages are clearly identifiable as the official source. Use Organization schema, consistent branding, verified social profiles, and a Knowledge Panel to signal official status.

Align with FreshnessTwiddler for time-sensitive content: FreshnessTwiddler boosts recent content for queries with time-sensitive intent. If your content has a freshness component (news, trends, seasonal topics, annual guides), update it with genuine new information before the relevant period. Simply changing the publication date without substantive updates does not trigger freshness signals since the pipeline distinguishes significantUpdate from cosmetic changes.

Understand that most ranking is hand-crafted, not AI: Only RankBrain and DeepRank use ML/LLM technologies (HJ Kim deposition). Everything else is hand-crafted signals combined via linear weighted formulas with sigmoid functions. This means ranking is more predictable and mechanistic than Google implies. Signals have specific thresholds and weights tuned by engineers. Below Q* 0.4, you are ineligible for rich results. These are concrete thresholds you can measure against.

Earn IS (Information Satisfaction) scores from rater patterns: 16,000 human raters score IS on a 0-100 scale, which trains RankBrain, SpamBrain, HelpfulContent, and MUM. These raters follow public Quality Rater Guidelines. Study the guidelines to understand what a high IS score looks like: expertise signals, comprehensive answers, good page experience, and trustworthy sourcing. Your content should satisfy a trained rater's checklist.

calculations.name: Mustang
calculations.source: DOJ: Initial retrieval and first-pass scoring
calculations.how: First-pass scoring system operating at massive scale. Reduces 400B indexed documents to tens of thousands of candidates using lightweight signals (T* topicality, basic quality filters). Mehta opinion (FOF 31, Nayak): 'the GSE must include a retrieval system that narrows the volume of responsive links to tens of thousands, as opposed to millions.' Then 'must decide which results are worth scoring at a more granular level, and then score those hundreds of sites to determine which top 10 or so should be surfaced to the user.' Google classifies queries into more than two dozen 'level-one' classifications (FOF 34).
calculations.formula: Mustang(query) = retrieve( Alexandria[400B docs], T*, quality_filters ) → tens of thousands // Nayak: narrows millions to tens of thousands → score(hundreds) → top 10 // then scores hundreds for final 10 // 2 dozen+ level-one query classifications (FOF 34)
calculations.affects: Affected by: basic relevance signals. Title-query match, body content relevance, basic topicality. Must pass this filter to be considered at all. Query classification determines which signals and features apply.

calculations.name: Twiddlers
calculations.how: Series of re-ranking functions applied post-Mustang. PredocTwiddlers (hundreds of URLs, fast heuristics for dedup/diversity). LazyTwiddlers (top 20-30 results, full metadata, fine-grained adjustments). Each twiddler is a separate mini-algorithm.
calculations.formula: PredocTwiddlers(candidates) → filter( dedup, diversity, DMCA ) // hundreds of URLs, fast heuristics LazyTwiddlers(top_results) → refine( full_metadata ) // top 20-30 only, expensive ops
calculations.affects: Affected by: different for each twiddler. OfficialPageTwiddler boosts brand pages. FreshnessTwiddler promotes recent content. YouTubeDensityTwiddler manages video density.

calculations.name: SuperRoot
calculations.how: Orchestration layer managing search pipeline flow. Routes queries through QUS > Mustang > Ascorer > Twiddlers > Tangram. Not a ranking signal itself but controls which signals are applied when.
calculations.formula: SuperRoot(query) → route( QUS → Mustang → Ascorer → Twiddlers → Tangram ) // orchestration, not a ranking signal // controls which signals apply at each stage
calculations.affects: Affected by: not directly actionable. Understanding the pipeline helps optimize for the right stage.

calculations.name: LocalInterConnectivity
calculations.how: Re-ranks initial search results based on inter-connectivity within the result set. Documents frequently cited by other high-scoring documents in the result set receive boosted rankings. Removes documents from same/affiliated hosts to prevent manipulation, then calculates LocalScore from the OldScores of linking documents. Final score combines original ranking with local connectivity support. The top k backlinking documents contribute, with a sensitivity parameter m controlling how strongly high-authority cross-references dominate.
calculations.formula: LocalScore(x) = sum( OldScore(BackSet(i))m for i in top_k ) // k = top backlinking docs in result set // m = sensitivity parameter (1-3) // same-host links excluded (anti-manipulation) NewScore(x) = (a + LocalScore / MaxLS) × (b + OldScore / MaxOS) // combines original score with local connectivity
calculations.patents: Patent: US6725259 (Ranking search results by reranking based on local inter-connectivity, 2003)
calculations.affects: Affected by: how many other top-ranking pages cite your page, the authority of those citing pages, host diversity of backlinks within the result set. Pages that are 'hubs' cited by multiple result-set documents benefit.

calculations.name: LinearWeightedFormula
calculations.source: DOJ: 100+ signals combined via linear weights
calculations.how: 100+ raw signals combined into top-level scores using linear weighted formulas. Nayak (PXR0357, Jan 2025): 'Top-level signals are a linear combination of log of individual raw signals.' Signals are log-transformed before linear combination, and 'formulated such that their impact on ranking is monotonic relative to the signal.' HJ Kim (PXR0356, Feb 2025): engineers 'take a sigmoid or other function and figure out the threshold.' For most signals, Google takes relevant data and performs a regression. In the extreme, hand-crafting means manually picking the midpoint. Google's baseline was Okapi BM25.
calculations.formula: Score(doc) = sum( wi * sigmoid(log(raw_signal_i)) for i in 100+ signals ) // log-transform then sigmoid (Nayak PXR0357) // monotonicity constraint on all signals // weights tuned by engineers, NOT learned // baseline: Okapi BM25 style ranking
calculations.affects: Affected by: performing well across multiple signals. No single signal dominates. Balanced optimization across quality, relevance, and engagement.

stages.name: Mustang
stages.detail: Retrieval: millions → tens of thousands (Nayak, Mehta FOF 31)

stages.name: Ascorer
stages.detail: Scores hundreds of candidates: Q* + P* + T* → top 10 (Mehta FOF 31)

stages.name: NavBoost
stages.detail: Early-stage click filter: culls tens of thousands to hundreds (not a final twiddler). Cannot rank docs without click history

stages.name: SERP Delivery
stages.detail: SRP served in 4 chunks: header, body, footer, late footer (UPX2022). Logged-in users +350ms latency. Mobile +50ms server-side

timeline.title: Mehta Opinion: Pipeline Architecture Confirmed (Aug 2024)
timeline.desc: Judge Mehta's opinion confirmed the full pipeline: retrieval narrows responsive links from millions to 'tens of thousands' (Nayak, FOF 31), then 'score those hundreds of sites to determine which top 10 or so should be surfaced.' Google uses 2 dozen+ 'level-one' query classifications (FOF 34). 78% of users search within only one vertical in short sessions (FOF 34). Only RankBrain and DeepRank use ML; all other signals are hand-crafted. LLMs are 'additional signals that get balanced' against others (Nayak, FOF 102).

timeline.title: Google vs Bing: Serving Architecture (UPX2022, DX0099)
timeline.desc: Internal analysis: SRP delivered in exactly 4 chunks (header, body, footer, late footer). Bing ~300ms faster server-side. Logged-in queries cost ~350ms extra (Bing: ~100ms). Mobile adds ~50ms server-side. Google SRP payload double Bing's size (~207kb vs ~112kb). Click tracking uses ~50-100 compressed bytes/URL via onmousedown rwt() rewrite. Project Folly launched to close gap. v2-xs model (2024): latency cut from 1628ms to 1370ms while doubling model size (PXR0037).

timeline.title: Rankable Gemini Suggestions (PXR0109)
timeline.desc: Gemini in Search exec review: 'Provide rankable Gemini suggestions depending on query.' Implies Gemini outputs enter the ranking pipeline as candidates alongside organic results, not bypassing it.

timeline.title: Ranking for Research: Secrecy and Scope (UPX0204)
timeline.desc: Eric Lehman's internal document: 'Attempts to manipulate search results are continuous, sophisticated, and well-funded.' Policies: 'Do not discuss the use of clicks in search, except on a need-to-know basis' and 'Do not discuss political bias in search in writing.' Lists 18 search quality aspects.

timeline.title: Ranking as Extreme Business Outlier (UPX0219)
timeline.desc: Eric Lehman (May 2020): 'Ranking is an extreme outlier in business impact.' 'Many search features use web results to understand what a query is about and trigger accordingly.' 'Technologies developed in search spread out across the company to Ads, YouTube, Play.' Ranking is Google's core competitive engine.

timeline.title: Pipeline Debugging Interface Revealed (PXR0357)
timeline.desc: Nayak interview (Jan 2025): Described internal debugging interface showing query expansion/decomposition and table of blue links with per-signal scores. Over 100 raw signals aggregate into top-level scores. Google deliberately avoids 'predicting clicks' because clicks are easily manipulated and a poor proxy for user experience.

contradictions.publicClaim: "Our ranking is powered by advanced AI and machine learning."
contradictions.internalClaim: Only RankBrain and DeepRank use ML/LLM. The vast majority of signals are hand-crafted. 100+ raw signals combined via linear weighted formulas.

Nayak testified there are 'maybe over a hundred' signals, down from historical 200+. Three top-level scores (Q*, P*, T*) dominate. T* has only 3 sub-signals (A, B, C). Most claimed "factors" are sub-components of these three scores. Even Google's own VP contradicts the 200+ marketing claim.

contradictions.publicClaim: "We don't use clicks to rank search results."
contradictions.internalSource: DOJ Trial Exhibit UPX0204 (Eric Lehman, Nov 2018)
contradictions.internalClaim: 'Do not discuss the use of clicks in search, except on a need-to-know basis. Google has a public position.' Internal secrecy policy explicitly designed to maintain the public denial of click usage in ranking.

contradictions.publicClaim: "Our search results are not politically biased. Algorithms don't have political leanings."
contradictions.internalSource: DOJ Trial Exhibit UPX0204 (Eric Lehman, Nov 2018)
contradictions.internalClaim: 'Do not discuss political bias in search in writing.' The policy to avoid written discussion of political bias suggests awareness of bias considerations that contradict the public position of neutrality.
